 Order

This appeal by the claimants under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 28.02.2017 passed by Addl. MACT, Khargone (WN) in Claim Case No.109/2015 seeking enhancement of the amount of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
2. The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Tribunal in this regard are also not in question.

As per the findings of the Tribunal,
for the death of Muskan, the Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.7,15,700/- along with interest.

The break up of the compensation amount is as under:
L o s s o f d e p e n d e n c y - R s . 5 , 8 3 , 2 0 0 / - ( i . e . R s . 5 4 0 0 - 5 0 % p e r s o n a l expenses=2700x12=32400x18 (multiplier)) Funeral expenses -Rs.25,000/-
 Transportation -Rs.5,000/-
 Loss of consortium -Rs.1,00,000/-
 Loss of estate -Rs.2,500/-
 -----------------
 TOTAL Rs.7,15,700/-
 ===========

3. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in awarding just and proper amount of compensation in the case as the amount awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
The Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding any amount under the head of future prospects in the light of the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Pranay Sethi.
The compensation under the head of other conventional heads also deserves to be enhanced, hence prays for just and proper amount of compensation in the case.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has argued in support of the impugned award and contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation amount in the case which does not call for any interference by this Court.
5. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, I find substance in the arguments advanced by the counsel for the appellant.

The deceased was aged about 18 years at the time of the accident, however, the Tribunal has not awarded any amount under the head of future prospects in the light of the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Pranay Sethi.
Considering the facts and Leeladhar vs Burahnuddin Ali @ Burhan on 13 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178395459/

2 circumstances of the case, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal deserves to be enhanced as under:
L o s s o f d e p e n d e n c y - R s . 5 , 8 3 , 2 0 0 / - ( i . e . R s . 5 4 0 0 - 5 0 % p e r s o n a l expenses=2700x12=32400x18 (multiplier)) Future prospects -Rs.2,33,280/- (40%)
Loss of consortium -Rs.88,000/- (44000x2) Funeral expenses -Rs.16,500/-
 Loss of estate -Rs.16,500/-
 Transportation -Rs.5,000/-
 -------------------
 TOTAL Rs.9,42,480/-
 ============
6.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the case is Rs.9,42,480/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.7,15,700/-.
Accordingly, the appellants are entitled to an additional sum of Rs.2,26,780/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
7. Accordingly, the appeal is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.2,26,780/-.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE hk/
